ratings.concept: Hierarchy of genetic organisation by containment: genome contains chromosomes, a chromosome contains genes, a gene is a run of nucleotides
ratings.strategy_evidence: The one fact that the genome is the whole of an organism's genetic material, so nothing can contain it, strikes out options 1 and 2, which both open with 'Chromosome'.

traps.label: sequence_endpoint_or_adjacency
traps.route: 'Genome, chromosomes, nucleotide, gene' gets the first two positions right and inverts the final adjacency, printing nucleotide before gene; the adjacency that fails is gene-nucleotide, a gene being a stretch of many nucleotides

traps.label: sequence_endpoint_or_adjacency
traps.route: 'Chromosome, genome, nucleotide, gene' inverts two adjacencies at once, the opening genome-chromosome pair and the closing gene-nucleotide pair, so both ends of the printed order are wrong while the middle pair is in contact

traps.label: no_derivation_route
traps.route: 'Chromosome, gene, genome, nucleotide' places the genome third, below gene, although the genome contains both the chromosomes and the genes named above it; no containment relation can order a whole after two of its parts, so no route from largest to smallest reaches this arrangement

ratings.reason: This question requires applying the containment relation to four named levels and reading off their order, demonstrated by the stem's 'from largest to smallest' and by option 4's 'Genome, chromosome, gene, nucleotide'.
ratings.note: The three wrong options are generated by two independent swaps crossed with each other - genome against chromosome at the top, gene against nucleotide at the bottom - with option 3 taking the second swap, option 1 both, and option 2 breaking the pattern. That grid is recorded here rather than as complementary_grid, because that label describes the option set as a whole while a trap entry must name one option, and each option is better served by the adjacency it actually fails. has_figure is true with figure_image at figures_agent/2015_A/q116.png; the stem and options are complete as text and need no figure.

ratings.concept: Neurohypophysis: ADH and oxytocin are synthesised in the hypothalamus and only stored and released by the posterior pituitary, while the anterior pituitary makes its own hormones
ratings.strategy_evidence: The one fact that the posterior pituitary synthesises no hormone of its own, so the hormone sought must be a neurohypophyseal one, strikes out options 1, 3 and 4, all adenohypophyseal hormones made in the gland itself.

traps.label: condition_ignored
traps.route: 'Melanocyte stimulating hormone' is released by the pituitary and is right as soon as the stem's condition 'though synthesis elsewhere' is dropped; MSH is made in the gland, so it satisfies the question only in the reading that ignores where synthesis happens

traps.label: condition_ignored
traps.route: 'Luteinizing hormone' is likewise released by the pituitary and is correct only with the same condition dropped: LH is synthesised by the anterior pituitary itself

traps.label: condition_ignored
traps.route: 'Prolactin' is the third adenohypophyseal hormone on the list, again released by the master gland and synthesised in it, so it too is right only once 'though synthesis elsewhere' is set aside

ratings.reason: This question requires a stated condition to decide which of several true pituitary hormones qualifies, demonstrated by the stem's 'though synthesis elsewhere, is stored and released by the master gland', without which every one of the four options is a hormone the pituitary releases.
ratings.note: condition_based_reasoning rather than recall, because removing the printed phrase 'though synthesis elsewhere' makes three other options correct; the rulebook's matching trap for that demand, condition_ignored, is what all three wrong options carry. The stem's 'though synthesis elsewhere' is printed with 'synthesis' where 'synthesised' is meant - a transcription or printing slip that does not change what the condition states.

ratings.concept: Joints classified by mobility: fibrous joints such as the skull sutures are immovable, cartilaginous joints slightly movable, synovial joints freely movable
ratings.strategy_evidence: The one fact that a ball-and-socket joint is a kind of synovial joint strikes out options 1 and 4 together, since two options that cannot be separated from each other cannot hold the single answer the stem asks for.

traps.label: other_one_fact
traps.route: 'Cartilaginous joint' is the adjacent member of the same mobility classification: cartilaginous joints such as those between adjacent vertebrae permit limited movement, so the fact offered is the one belonging to the slightly movable class rather than the immovable one

traps.label: other_one_fact
traps.route: 'Synovial joint' is the freely movable member of the same classification, its fluid-filled cavity being what permits movement

traps.label: other_one_fact
traps.route: 'Ball and Socket joint' is a named instance of that same freely movable class, the shoulder and hip joints

ratings.reason: This question requires one stored fact about one class of joint, demonstrated by the stem 'Which of the following joints would allow no movement?' and option 2's bare 'Fibrous joint', the sutures between skull bones.
ratings.note: Options 1 and 4 are not mutually exclusive as printed: a ball-and-socket joint is a synovial joint, so one option is contained in the other. That is a property of the printed option set, not of our storage, so no source damage verdict is recorded; it is noted because it is what the elimination shortcut above exploits.

ratings.concept: Chargaff's equivalence rule (A equals T, G equals C) holds for double-stranded DNA and not for single-stranded RNA, which still shows base pairing, 5' to 3' polarity and heterocyclic bases

traps.label: true_statement_trap
traps.route: 'Complementary base pairing' is applicable to RNA - tRNA cloverleaf arms and codon-anticodon pairing are both complementary pairings - and so fails the stem's negated task, 'not applicable to RNA'

traps.label: true_statement_trap
traps.route: '5' phosphoryl and 3' hydroxyl ends' is true of RNA as of any polynucleotide and fails the same negated polarity

traps.label: true_statement_trap
traps.route: 'Heterocyclic nitrogenous bases' is true of RNA, whose purines and pyrimidines are heterocyclic rings, and fails the same negated polarity

ratings.reason: This question requires holding a property specific to double-stranded DNA apart from properties shared by both nucleic acids, demonstrated by option 1's 'Chargaff's rule', which states an equivalence between the two strands of a duplex that single-stranded RNA has no second strand to satisfy.
ratings.note: concept_discrimination rather than recall because the decision is which of four true-sounding nucleic-acid properties is DNA-specific, which is a DNA-against-RNA discrimination rather than a single stored fact. Structure is several_independent_checks because the task is negated and each property has to be tested against RNA separately.

ratings.concept: Heart sounds: the first sound is the atrioventricular valves closing at the start of ventricular systole, the second the semilunar valves closing at its end

traps.label: semantic_reversal
traps.route: 'AV valves open up' prints the opposite action of the valves whose closing makes the first heart sound; opening the AV valves is silent, and the reversed word is 'open' where the sound-producing event is closure

traps.label: wrong_site_or_stage
traps.route: 'Ventricular walls vibrate due to gushing of blood from atria' moves the event to the wrong stage of the cycle: the offered stage is ventricular filling from the atria, in diastole, while the second sound is produced at the end of ventricular systole, at the semilunar valves

traps.label: true_but_out_of_scope
traps.route: 'AV node receives signal from SA node' is a real event of the cardiac cycle and fails on relevance: the stem asks what is heard through a stethoscope, and the passage of the impulse from the SA to the AV node is electrical and silent

ratings.reason: This question requires one stored fact about which mechanical event produces one named sound, demonstrated by option 4's 'Semilunar valves close down after the blood flows into vessels from ventricles'.

ratings.concept: Ecological succession: a gradual and predictable change in species composition running from the pioneer community to the climax community

traps.label: single_word_substitution
traps.route: 'The changes lead to a community that is in near equilibrium with the environment and is called pioneer community' is correct in every word except one noun: the community in near equilibrium with the environment is the climax community, and 'pioneer' names the first community of the sequence instead, with the surrounding sentence standing correct around the swapped word

traps.label: semantic_reversal
traps.route: 'The establishment of a new biotic community is very fast in its primary phase' prints the rate the other way round: primary succession on a bare substrate is the slow phase, since soil has to form first; the reversed words are 'very fast' for what the textbook has as slow

traps.label: semantic_reversal
traps.route: 'The number and types of animals remain constant' asserts constancy of the very thing succession is defined as changing; the reversed words are 'remain constant' against the key's 'change in species composition'

ratings.reason: This question requires one stored definition, demonstrated by option 2's 'The gradual and predictable change in species composition occurs in a given area', which is the definition of succession stated outright.
ratings.note: Structure is single_step and not several_independent_checks: the task polarity is direct and one recalled definition settles it. That option 1 is a near-identical sentence with one noun swapped is a device on the trap axis, not extra structure in the solution - which is the separation the rulebook's rebuild of this axis was for.

group_note: Six questions grouped on the printed shape 'plain'. One member does not sit with the rest on shape: q116 asks for an ordering ('from largest to smallest') and its options are orders, not claims, so a later pass should expect an order-shaped answer form there; the other five are single-claim options. Structure was set by one test applied to all six - does the task force a verdict on more than one item? q116 does, because an order of four levels is three adjacencies each adjudicated, and q120 does, because its task is negated ('not applicable to RNA') and a negated task cannot be settled without testing every option; those two are several_independent_checks. The remaining four are single_step, each settled by one stored fact, and none is multi_step_dependent since nowhere does one result feed the next. Demand was set by asking what the live decision is. q116 applies the containment relation to named levels, which is application. q117 is the one member whose decision is a printed condition: strike 'though synthesis elsewhere' from the stem and three other options become correct, which is condition_based_reasoning, and its matching trap, condition_ignored, is what those three options carry - this is why q117 is not recall even though one fact about ADH settles it. q120 is concept_discrimination, the decision being which of four true-sounding nucleic-acid properties belongs to duplex DNA alone. q119, q121 and q122 are recall, each a single taught fact - the immovable class of joint, the event behind the second heart sound, the definition of succession. q119 was kept at recall rather than concept_discrimination because the key is reached by knowing which class is immovable, not by holding two classes apart; the neighbouring classes are recorded on the trap axis as other_one_fact instead. Elimination appears three times, each with a named fact and named options: the genome containing everything (q116, striking options 1 and 2), the posterior pituitary synthesising nothing of its own (q117, striking 1, 3 and 4), and ball-and-socket being a synovial joint (q119, striking 1 and 4 as inseparable). It is withheld from q120, where striking the true options is the negated task's method rather than a shortcut, and from q121 and q122, where the only available fact is the answer itself. On the trap axis every wrong option in this packet carries a device, and the labels follow what is printed rather than a house style: true_statement_trap three times on q120, where the negated polarity makes every non-key option a true claim that fails the task; condition_ignored three times on q117, where each wrong option is right as soon as the printed condition is dropped; other_one_fact three times on q119, where each wrong option is another member of the same mobility classification; and on q116 the adjacency labels, with no_derivation_route used once and demonstrated from containment rather than asserted. q122's option 1 is the group's one single_word_substitution, a fluent and otherwise correct sentence with 'climax' replaced by 'pioneer'. No trap in this packet is placed on an official answer.
